How is Massachusetts organized when you sell a house?

Massachusetts has 14 counties and 351 municipalities, and the town or city you live in does more of the work than the county. Assessors, tax collectors, boards of health and fire departments are all local. Counties matter mainly for the registries of deeds.

Three local offices come up in nearly every sale:

  • The assessors, who set the value your tax bill is based on.
  • The tax collector, who takes payment and can tell you what is owed.
  • The registry of deeds, which records the deed that moves title to the buyer.

The state has 21 registry of deeds district offices, so some counties have more than one. Berkshire has three, Bristol has three, and Essex, Middlesex and Worcester have two each. For a wider list, see Massachusetts guides by city and county.

What do property taxes look like when you sell in Massachusetts?

Massachusetts cities and towns all run a fiscal year from July 1 to June 30, and the tax rate is usually not set until around October or November. Many towns bill quarterly. One town explains that the July and October bills are estimates, the January bill is the first actual one, and the April bill matches it.

The assessor builds the tax list and commits it to the collector. If you think your value is too high, the window to ask for an abatement is short. That same town allows it only during the first 30 days after the January bill goes out, and your own town may differ.

Unpaid tax usually has to be cleared out of the sale proceeds at closing, so ask the collector for a payoff figure before you set a closing date. Our Massachusetts property tax guide covers appeals and exemptions.

What does a Massachusetts closing involve, and do you need a lawyer?

In practice, yes. The Trial Court Law Libraries note that real estate attorneys are a regular part of buying and selling here, both by law and by custom. The state's highest court has also held that closings require the substantive participation of an attorney acting for the mortgage lender.

A lawyer usually handles the purchase and sale agreement, the title review, the payoff of your mortgage and the deed. Title also comes in two forms:

  • Recorded land, filed with the county registry. The court library says this covers 80 to 90 percent of properties.
  • Registered land, described on a Certificate of Title issued through the Land Court.

Registered land has extra recording rules. The Suffolk registry requires the seller to sign exactly as they took title and does not accept AKA or NKA names. Check which type you own before the deed is drafted.

State rules also restrict how sellers treat inspections. Under 760 CMR 74, sellers of certain residential properties cannot make an offer conditional on the buyer waiving a home inspection.

How much is the deed excise tax and what does recording cost?

The deeds excise tax is $2.28 for each $500 of consideration, or fraction of it, on deeds where the consideration is more than $100. The Suffolk registry publishes a calculator. It is paid by separate check from the recording fee, and the registry wants the recording fee check in the exact amount.

ItemWhat the registry says
Excise rate$2.28 per $500 or fraction of consideration
Applies whenConsideration is more than $100
PaymentExcise on a separate check from recording fees
Fee checkExact amount, payable to Commonwealth of Massachusetts
PrivacyRedact Social Security numbers before recording

Who pays the excise is a point your purchase and sale agreement should settle in writing, so ask your attorney. Our recording a deed guide and quitclaim deed guide give more detail.

How does foreclosure work in Massachusetts?

Most Massachusetts foreclosures are nonjudicial. Lenders can go through the courts, but the Trial Court Law Libraries say foreclosure by power of sale is the more common route, and the procedure sits in G.L. c. 244, section 14.

The timing rules are specific:

  • The sale notice must run once a week for three successive weeks, and the first notice must appear at least 21 days before the sale.
  • The owner must be sent notice by registered mail at least 14 days before the sale.
  • Before the lender can accelerate or enforce, most owner-occupied homes with four or fewer households get a 90-day right to cure. It can be used once in any five-year period.

The cure notice must also describe options to sell, refinance or deed the property in lieu of foreclosure, so selling is a recognized path, not a last resort. Greater Boston Legal Services is one free resource the state names.

How do you sell an inherited house in Massachusetts?

Probate runs through the Probate and Family Court, and the route depends on the estate. Informal probate is handled by a magistrate without hearings, and an order can issue as early as 7 days after death. Formal probate is usually heard by a judge, and it applies when someone objects, the will is a copy or is unclear, or informal probate is not available.

Real estate changes the picture:

  • Voluntary administration, the simple process for small estates, is only for personal property worth $25,000 or less. It does not cover real estate.
  • A personal representative in a late and limited proceeding cannot get a license to sell the decedent's real estate.
  • Letters of Authority only issue after the representative is appointed and a bond is approved.

If you are an heir with no appointment yet, you cannot simply sign a deed. Start with the probate registry for the county where the person lived. Read our Massachusetts probate guide and estate tax guide, and ask the court clerk about timing.

What does the homestead protection mean for a seller?

The state's homestead statute lists two exemptions: an automatic one of $125,000, and a declared one of $1,000,000 created by a written declaration that is recorded. Owners of single-family homes, two to four family homes, condos and manufactured homes can qualify, and no one may hold rights in more than one principal residence.

For a seller, the main question is whether a declaration is on record. A recorded declaration shows up in a title search and your attorney will want to deal with it before the deed. Our homestead guide covers how it works in a sale.

What property problems come up on Massachusetts sales?

Two rules catch sellers by surprise, and both involve local officials.

The first is septic. Homes with a private system generally need a Title 5 inspection within two years before the sale. If weather blocks the inspection, it can be done within six months after the sale if the seller notifies the buyer in writing. A passing report is generally good for two years, or three if the system is pumped every year. A failed system must be upgraded within two years unless the board of health agrees to another schedule, and cesspools and soil absorption systems cannot be fixed under a conditional pass.

The second is smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. Under M.G.L. c. 148, section 26F, the fire department inspects when a one or two family home is sold and issues a Certificate of Compliance. Alarms cannot be older than 10 years. Fees are set by each town, and the guide says to call the fire department as soon as a closing date is set.

IssueWho handles itTiming
Title 5 septic inspectionProperty owner, with the local board of healthWithin 2 years before sale
Smoke and CO alarm certificateLocal fire departmentSchedule as soon as closing date is set
Tax payoffLocal tax collectorAsk before closing
Deed recordingCounty registry of deedsAfter closing

An as-is cash sale does not erase these items. If the house also has tenants, read our landlord and tenant guide and eviction notice guide before you list.

What does selling as-is for cash mean in Massachusetts?

It means the buyer takes the house in its current condition and does not ask you to repair or update it. You still need clear title, a recorded deed and the local certificates above, so a cash sale mostly removes the financing and showing steps, not the paperwork.

Before you accept any offer, read the purchase and sale agreement with your attorney, confirm who pays the excise tax, and ask how the buyer will handle septic and alarm certificates. We buy directly or bring a vetted cash buyer, and we do not promise a price before we see the property.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties does Massachusetts have?

There are 14 counties and 351 municipalities. Deeds are recorded at one of 21 registry of deeds district offices.

Do I need a lawyer to sell a house in Massachusetts?

The state court library says attorneys are a regular part of home sales by law and by custom.

What is the deed excise tax rate?

It is $2.28 for each $500 of consideration, or fraction of it. Ask your attorney who pays it under your contract.

Is foreclosure in Massachusetts handled by a court?

Usually not. Power of sale is the more common method, and many owner-occupied homes get a 90-day right to cure first.

Can I sell inherited property before probate approval?

Not safely. A personal representative must be appointed and bonded, and voluntary administration excludes real estate.

Do I need a septic inspection to sell?

With a private system, generally yes, within two years before the sale.

What is the smoke alarm certificate?

The local fire department inspects alarms on one and two family home sales and issues a Certificate of Compliance.
